item.title: SCP idea- Borrasca: Re: SCP idea- Borrasca
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. As a general note, this line:

the elevator pitch is the attention grabber

immediately made me skeptical, because "the basic explanation of the idea" isn't really something that would grab a reader's attention when reading a full article. When identifying the material that is supposed to stick in a reader's memory and keep them interested in reading, you want to think more about elements like the uniqueness of the story, an unexpected twist in an otherwise-standard formulaic approach, an introspective nature that will make a reader contemplate the nature of the anomaly, that sort of thing. Just "I think the entire thing grabs attention" with no reason given might come off as lazy and/or presumptive.

That said… the basic premise is fairly commonplace and also rather vague. The setup of a haunted industrial location suddenly starting to go back to its former production with no explanation feels like standard ghost story/urban legend fodder, and the fact that no one can explore it because typical Bad Things happen to them is fairly predictable. You would need to do more explaining of the more unique details in order to better convince readers that this isn't just a rehash of existing ghost stories. As such:

The first batch of coal came with a strange note: do not use within the town of [Redacted].

This leaves me as a reader with the question "So what?" The cryptic note on its own doesn't really pique much attention. What's the significance of the town (which for all I know could be on the other side of the world)? Why must there be a location limit for the coal use? Why did the townspeople decide to sell or store the coal rather than use it themselves? Also, if the mine was abandoned for years and suddenly started up again with no listed workers or management, how did no one get suspicious?

it will generally be about what happens if you use the coal in the town and what happens down in the mine

What happens if you use the coal in the town? What happens down in the mine?

item.title: Extreme Larping (seeking greenlight): Re: Extreme Larping (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
So does time stop when they roll, or does it keep going? If it doesn't then they could be taken out easily enough by making sure that they can't roll. If it does, then it could get weird.

They could also be trapped in the persona of their characters, making for some interesting problems, like the rogue having to steal someone every so often or the healer having to heal someone she would prefer not to. The personality conflict could be interesting to watch. Also, can they switch character sheets or could others use the sheets? Would they use the levels on the sheets or go back to Level 1?

Given the general grimness of the SCP universe, it would be interesting to see more fumbles than crits, making these guys more scared kids than expert adults, especially if they have a problem figuring out their new class abilities. Mages especially can create some chaos, especially given the possibilities of summoning demons or even other SCPs.

item.title: SCP-5144 Proposal: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: Reality Warping Anime Husbando VTuber (Seeking Greenlight): Re: Reality Warping Anime Husbando VTuber (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
1) The ethical and legal implications should be handled elsewhere. You may want to look at the admin panel to see who to discuss that with.

2) Details rock. There are some questions about what happens when he shifts to a new anime world; does he transform into a native or does he resemble himself? Would he gain power armor if he shifted to a mecha universe, or be in medieval wear if in an isekai anime? Would he gain powers in a superhero universe?

3) Why go meta? It's not a bad idea, but just because he can shift to different universes doesn't mean he needs to have a meta-perspective. I get the Deadpool connection, but unless you have an actual purpose for it, it just feels sort of tacked on. Also, his abilities don't exactly beg for it. It just feels like you want to do an anime thing on one hand and different realities on the other (and I'm not sure the SCP needs yet another dimension-hopper).

item.title: The Mushroom Men: Re: The Mushroom Men
item.content:encoded:
While there are a number of great ideas here, there's nothing really solid. Some of the ideas you have in the Elevator Pitch should be moved into the Central Narrative, and then you need to build up the Mushroom Men in terms of what they are, what kind of society they have, and why they are fighting SCP 610.

While we get an idea of what you are trying to do, the problem is that there is nothing really about the Mushroom Men themselves here, and with nothing here they're just a generic race for the sake of having a new race. Nail down some of the specifics, and then go for it. We don't need a thesis on them, just something to make them breathe (so to speak) a little.
